content: Is there any literature about tools for theorem proving such as simp, or toy implementations? Do tools like simp have a more general name? I'd like to study its internals and try a small implementation, but source's code is a bit overwhelming. Would anyone have tips? Thank you

nrs said:

Do tools like simp have a more general name?

Most commonly "automation tactics" / "hammers", but simp specifically is referred to as a "simplifier" / "confluent rewriting system".

AFAIK the term "hammer" originated in Isabelle and I believe it refers to "using a sledgehammer to crack a nut".
Though it might be debatable whether the term includes simp or not.
I see, that's enough to get started on a citation hunt, tyvm!
Ty for the answer, I wasn't quite sure whether I could use it as a reference, does it adequate with the manual's section on simp?

This tutorial covers an implementation of a toy simp in the file CustomSimp.lean (depending on your background you may want to do the other two tutorials there first)

https://github.com/mirefek/lean-tactic-programming-guide

Hammers refers to a specific kind of automation that invokes external solvers and uses their results to construct a proof in the original ITP, not just tactics in general
